Article Title: 'New pace, new height': PM Modi-Parmelin talks put India-Switzerland ties on fast track
Article Text:
File photo: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Swiss President Guy Parmelin at Hyderabad House for bilateral talks, in New Delhi on Monday

India eyes $100 billion investment under TEPA

Defence, nuclear energy and infrastructure on agenda

Parmelin calls visit a ‘stepping stone’

Swiss business delegation accompanies Parmelin

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Swiss Confederation president Guy Parmelin held wide-ranging talks in New Delhi on Monday, with the two sides discussing ways to deepen cooperation in trade and investment, mobility, infrastructure, defence, nuclear energy and critical technologies.The talks came as India and Switzerland seek to build on the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA), which entered into force last October and is set to complete a year of implementation this week.Addressing a joint press statement after the talks, PM Modi said the relationship between India and Switzerland had gained fresh momentum and highlighted the two countries' cooperation in innovation, infrastructure and advanced technology.“India-Switzerland friendship is centuries-old... Innovation, infrastructure and advanced technology are strong pillars of our foundation today. With the Summit today, we are going to give a new pace and height to our partnership,” PM Modi said.PM Modi said TEPA was an ambitious blueprint for investment, innovation, jobs and shared prosperity and set out a target of attracting $100 billion in investment into India and creating 1 million direct jobs over the next 15 years.“I am very happy to welcome the president of Switzerland to India. First of all, I would like to appreciate his commitment to India-Switzerland relations. With his personal support, last October we implemented a historic Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement between India and the European Free Trade Association, or EFTA, countries,” PM Modi said.“This is India's first FTA with any economic bloc in Europe,” he added.The Prime Minister said India and Switzerland had also taken decisions to increase market access for Indian exports to Switzerland and facilitate investment between the two countries.He said the measures would support exports of Indian agricultural products, pharmaceuticals, textiles and engineering goods, while encouraging Swiss investment in sectors including biotechnology, life sciences, banking, insurance, food processing and sustainability.The talks also expanded beyond trade and investment, with PM Modi saying the two countries had identified new opportunities for military exchanges and defence production cooperation.“We also agreed to further deepen nuclear energy cooperation,” he said.PM Modi pointed to projects such as the Varanasi ropeway, Noida's Jewar airport and railway and tunnelling projects in mountainous regions as examples of India-Switzerland infrastructure cooperation.The two sides also signed an agreement covering transport, mobility and infrastructure, with PM Modi inviting Swiss infrastructure companies to increase investment in India and participate in capacity-building, design and manufacturing.People-to-people ties were another focus of the discussions. PM Modi said the Migration and Mobility Partnership Agreement and Young Professionals Agreement signed during the visit would create new opportunities in Switzerland for Indian students, researchers, professionals and young people.Parmelin, who is on a three-day State visit to India, described the trip as an opportunity to further strengthen the long-standing relationship between the two countries.He said India and Switzerland shared democratic values as well as trust and mutual respect, and described his visit as a “stepping stone” towards deepening their partnership.The Swiss president's visit is also significant for TEPA, which was signed in March 2024 after nearly 16 years of negotiations and came into force in October 2025. The EFTA countries — Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway — have committed to investing $100 billion in India over 15 years under the agreement.Parmelin is scheduled to attend the second India-EFTA Prosperity Summit on October 7, marking the first anniversary of TEPA's implementation.Parmelin arrived in New Delhi earlier on Monday and was accorded a ceremonial reception at Rashtrapati Bhavan before visiting Rajghat to pay tribute to Mahatma Gandhi. He was accompanied by a delegation of senior officials and business representatives.External affairs minister S Jaishankar also met Parmelin and said he appreciated the Swiss president's commitment to deepening the India-Switzerland partnership and building on the promise of TEPA.According to the ministry of external aaffairs, Switzerland is India's largest trade and investment partner among the four EFTA countries.More than 330 Swiss companies currently operate in India across sectors including engineering, services, precision instruments, chemicals and pharmaceuticals, while Indian companies in Switzerland have a presence in areas including IT, pharmaceuticals and machinery.Parmelin will also meet President Droupadi Murmu, who is scheduled to host a banquet in his honour. The visit is his first State visit to India and his second trip to the country this year, after his participation in the AI Impact Summit in New Delhi in February.
Article Summary: Prime minister narendra modi and swiss confederation president guy parmelin held wide-ranging talks in new delhi on monday. The two sides discussed ways to deepen cooperation in trade and investment, mobility, infrastructure, defence, nuclear energy and critical technologies.

Sharing details of the meeting on X, Jaishankar said he appreciated Parmelin's sentiments towards deepening the India-Switzerland partnership and building on the promise of the India-EFTA TEPA.“Confident that his meeting with PM Narendra Modi will further our engagement across a wide range of domains,” Jaishankar said.Parmelin began his official itinerary with a ceremonial reception at Rashtrapati Bhavan, where he was received by President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Modi.Speaking to the media after the welcome ceremony, Parmelin described his visit as an opportunity to underline the importance both countries attach to their relationship.“The visit is an excellent opportunity to emphasise the importance that both Switzerland and India attach to this relationship,” he said.He said India-Switzerland ties were based on “shared democratic values as well as on trust and mutual respect”.“My visit is a stepping stone towards further growth, deepening and strengthening of our close, broad and long-standing partnership,” Parmelin said.He also highlighted the significance of the first anniversary of TEPA's implementation, saying it was a moment to assess the progress made by the two sides while looking towards future cooperation.“It is the right moment to celebrate how far we have come together, but even more importantly, to shape our joint future,” he said.During his three-day visit, Parmelin is expected to hold discussions with Indian leaders on trade, investment, science and technology, innovation, mobility, cultural exchanges and people-to-people ties. Among the four EFTA countries, Switzerland is India's largest trade and investment partner, according to the Ministry of External Affairs.“India and Switzerland share longstanding friendly relations. This visit will further strengthen bilateral relations, building upon the regular high-level exchanges and deepen cooperation in new areas of mutual interest,” the MEA said.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: Trump says "125 million indians voted in presidential election today." However, india did not hold a presidential election on sunday. The president of india is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote. Trump's remarks came after brazil held the first round of its presidential election.

Article Title: ‘Gyanesh must quit right away': Opposition backs Justice Bhuyan’s 'SIR strikes at Constitution's heart' remark
Article Text:
Opposition backs Supreme Court of India Judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan

'No amount of whataboutery can justify'

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh and Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra backed Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan after his remarks on voting rights and the disenfranchisement of citizens at an event in Hyderabad.Sharing a video of Bhuyan’s speech in an X post, Ramesh targeted chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and said that Bhuyan had “exposed the CEC lock, stock and barrel”.He also called on Kumar to quit, alleging that his ability to execute what he described as “G2’s illegal orders” had made him “a liability for the country”.TMC MP Mahua Moitra also praised the judge, saying it was rare for a sitting judge to “speak truth to power”. “Kudos to Justice Bhuyan,” she said.Speaking at NALSAR University of Law on Sunday, Bhuyan said the right to vote is integral to the basic structure of the Constitution. He said any process that results in the disenfranchisement of millions of Indian citizens, making them “second-class citizens in their own country” without voting rights, would be intrinsically arbitrary.“No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution,” he said.Bhuyan further said the Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens, those with voting rights and those without them — and that wholesale disenfranchisement would violate Articles 14 and 326. He also said the right to vote or be included in the voters' list cannot be detached from a citizen’s status, comparing it to “taking out the soul from the body”.His remarks came amid the ongoing political and legal controversy over the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Article Summary: Opposition backs supreme court of india judge justice ujjal bhuyan. He said any process that results in the disenfranchisement of millions of indian citizens would be intrinsically arbitrary. Congress leader jairam ramesh and trinamool congress mp mahua moitra backed the judge.

Article Title: 1 dead as Russian drones hit desi pharma plant in Ukraine
Article Text:
Smoke comes out from a pharma plant struck in Ukraine’s Sumy on Sunday

Six Russian drones struck an Indian pharma plant in Ukraine’s Sumy Sunday in what Kusum Group cofounder Sanjeev Gupta described as a “targeted attack”, killing an engineer and injuring some others. The main structure of the facility was largely destroyed.Speaking to TOI, Gupta said the attack was not an isolated incident and claimed that pharmaceutical and food facilities in Ukraine had also come under attack over the past month. “Six drones hit the factory. So, it is a targeted attack. It’s not by chance. Actually, for the last one month, they are attacking all pharma and food items also,” Gupta said.The plant was operational when the strikes took place, Gupta said. The engineering department was hit and one engineer was killed, while other workers were evacuated.Gupta said the extent of damage could keep the plant out of operation for at least one to two years.“We are not able to evaluate the losses right now. We will come to know more tomorrow. But as per my understanding, we will not run this plant in the near future,” he added.In a statement issued later Sunday, Kusum Healthcare Pvt Ltd said total damage from the attack was projected to breach the $50 million mark.The company said its India business and management were reviewing the situation as the extent of the destruction emerged. The Sumy facility covers around 50,000 sq metres and has five blocks, Gupta said.It has been manufacturing medicines in Ukraine since 2009, including products for segments such as cardiology and gastroenterology. Gupta said Kusum is the biggest Indian pharmaceutical company operating in Ukraine, with a market share of more than 3%. The latest attack is not the first major strike on Kusum’s Ukrainian operations.The company said its warehouse was destroyed by a Russian drone on April 14, 2025, with losses from that attack exceeding UAH 1 billion.Despite the latest setback, Gupta said the group plans to continue its business in Ukraine.
Article Summary: Six russian drones struck an indian pharma plant in ukraine’s sumy sunday. Kusum group cofounder sanjeev gupta described it as a ‘targeted attack’ one engineer was killed, while other workers were evacuated. Total damage from the attack was projected to breach the $50 million mark.

Article Title: External affairs minister S Jaishankar says US has chosen to become 'lonelier power'

Article Title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Launching a scathing attack on special intensive revision (SIR) that has resulted in large-scale deletion of names from voter lists across states, Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution.Discounting the reasons given by govt and EC to justify SIR, which was upheld in the case of the revision of rolls in West Bengal by SC with modifications, Justice Bhuyan said, "No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of Constitution. I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution."He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad.Nalsar students, who had opposed CJI Surya Kant's participation in the convocation ceremony recently, came in for praise from Justice Bhuyan.Also read| Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman "One last word about the brilliant students of Nalsar. You have shown to the country and to the world what a university student, that too a student of law, should be. You are brilliant, you are bold, and you are brave," he said.Justice Bhuyan said a citizen’s right to vote was central to the holding of free and fair elections.“Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing,” he added.The SC judge said the right to vote or be included in the voters’ list could not be detached from the persona of an Indian citizen.Also read: EC orders special drive to add genuine electors 'left out' during SIR “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added. Justice Bhuyan said the Indian Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens: citizens with voting rights and citizens without voting rights. “Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution of India,” he said.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary,” he added, his remarks coinciding with attacks on EC and govt over SIR by the opposition and others.Justice Bhuyan said the right to vote was intertwined with India’s years of struggle against foreign rule. “It is a manifestation of our freedom achieved after so much struggle and sacrifice. Article 326 (universal adult franchise) cannot be tinkered with at all. No authority can do it, no court can condone it. No one is above Constitution,” he said.
Article Summary: Supreme court judge justice ujjal bhuyan on sunday said any process disenfranchising millions of indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary. He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at nalsar, hyderabad. “if it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added.

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Sunday said the global landscape was being shaped by a “radical repositioning” of the United States and the rise of China, while asserting that India has the potential to move rapidly up the global power hierarchy in the coming years.Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, Jaishankar said the US had “deliberately become a lonelier power” as part of a chosen change in its posture.“No one in the room would disagree with the fact that the landscape today is primarily marked by a radical repositioning of the United States. A repositioning which is a posture of choice and, in a way, it has deliberately become a lonelier power,” Jaishankar said.He identified the rise of China as the second major feature of the changing global order, pointing to the increasingly sharp competition between the two powers.“That competition today, not limited to these two countries, has led to a weaponization of any leverage that any country has. And that competition coexists with the complexity of interdependence,” he said.On India’s prospects, Jaishankar said the country had “decades of high growth” ahead and a demographic profile capable of supporting that growth.He also said India may not have to follow the traditional industrialisation path taken by earlier economies.“I would even argue, a world that is much more creative, where many new possibilities are there, so that we don't necessarily have to tread the earlier path of industrialization,” he said.“The orthodox path will have to devise something much more contemporary for what awaits us,” he added.Jaishankar said countries currently classified as middle powers could follow different trajectories as the global order evolves.“Among the middle powers, some will peel off, some will stay put, some may drop down a bit,” he said.“That is the reality. That will be part of the evolution of the global order,” Jaishankar added.The Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi is being held on October 4 and 5, bringing together senior decision-makers and experts to discuss international security and foreign policy issues.
Article Summary: Eam points to india’s growth, demographics as key global advantages. Jaishankar said the us had “deliberately become a lonelier power” as part of a chosen change in its posture. He identified the rise of china as the second major feature of the changing global order.

Article Title: ‘Unbelievable’: Sitharaman hits back at Jairam Ramesh's ‘public anger’ claim over viral Andhra clip

NEW DELHI: A political row erupted between the Congress and members of NDA after a video showing a brief interruption during Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman's speech in Andhra Pradesh's Madanapalle on October 2 went viral on social media.The 30-second clip showed Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu addressing the crowd during Sitharaman's speech. A social media user claimed that people in the gathering were demanding jobs. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh later reposted the clip and alleged that the crowd's reaction reflected public anger."The finance minister herself is seeing how much anger there is among the public. The chief minister had to silence the people," Ramesh said.Sitharaman rejected the Congress leader's interpretation, saying workers of the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and Jana Sena Party were eager to meet their leaders, Naidu and Pawan Kalyan, during the event.Calling Ramesh's conclusion "unbelievable", Sitharaman said Naidu had only asked the workers to wait until the programme ended before interacting with the leaders."Unbelievable, Jairam. Didn't think you were impetuous. The workers of both TDP and Jana Sena Party wanted to meet their leaders, Chandrababu Naidu and Pawan Kalyan.The chief minister only said they would meet them after the programme ended. That was all," Sitharaman said in the comment section of Ramesh's post.Naidu also hit back at Ramesh, saying the clip had been presented as evidence of public anger when the gathering had actually witnessed an enthusiastic response."Jairam ji, your interpretation of what happened could not be further from reality. What you are trying to falsely portray as public anger was, in fact, an overwhelming and enthusiastic response from the people. The sheer enthusiasm of the gathering required me to intervene briefly so that the programme could continue smoothly," Naidu said.State minister Nara Lokesh, who was present at the event, also criticised Ramesh, accusing him of promoting a false narrative without verifying the circumstances.Lokesh said there had been no protest among the crowd and alleged that a routine interaction with an enthusiastic gathering had been selectively presented to suggest public discontent.

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Sunday said that India has stepped beyond traditional advocacy to actively broker peace and operational agreements between Russia and Ukraine.During the Munich leaders meeting, Jaishankar said that India is actively holding conversations with Russia and Ukraine to end the war, which has stretched on for more than four years."Having said that, we are seeing today an unfortunate conflict. Our position on that conflict has been very clear, which is that we would like to see an end to this conflict. This will require dialogue and diplomacy. There has to be negotiations in this regard," Jaishankar said."We have been advocating it for many years, and in recent months we have got a little bit more involved beyond advocacy. We have conversations with both Russia and Ukraine in this regard. We are trying to be helpful, starting with the Black Sea safety of shipping issue, but going beyond that to cover some immediate concerns which both of them have on grain exports, energy exports, non-attack possibilities. Those are ongoing conversations right now," he added.This comes after a meeting of the consultative committee of the ministry of external affairs on India-Russia relations, where members reviewed New Delhi’s active engagement with both Moscow and Kyiv to help end hostilities.During the review, progress on major transit projects, energy cooperation and strategic connectivity was examined. India reaffirmed that its primary energy objective remains safeguarding the interests of Indian consumers, while both nations underscored a shared ambition to expand bilateral trade and investment in a balanced manner.India’s active mediation efforts have also been acknowledged by key figures on both sides of the conflict.Ukrainian foreign minister Andrii Sybiha confirmed that India has formally stepped forward to help resolve the conflict, offering what Kyiv considers “the most comprehensive” peace proposal currently under evaluation. Speaking at a press briefing, Sybiha said Kyiv was reviewing four distinct international proposals, including submissions from Turkey, Egypt and the United States.“We have four proposals. The most comprehensive is India’s proposal. For the first time, India has signalled its willingness to play a role,” Sybiha stated, as reported by RBC-Ukraine.Similarly, Russian President Vladimir Putin praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s efforts to help bring an end to the conflict, saying the Indian leader has “good ideas” for a peaceful resolution.Prime Minister Modi has consistently reiterated India’s principled and humanitarian approach to the crisis, maintaining that dialogue remains the only viable path to lasting peace.
Article Summary: External affairs minister s jaishankar said india has stepped beyond traditional advocacy to actively broker peace and operational agreements between russia and ukraine. This comes after a meeting of the consultative committee of the ministry of external affairs on india-russia relations, where members reviewed new delhi’s active engagement with both moscow and kyiv.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process that "disenfranchises millions of Indian citizens" is “intrinsically arbitrary” and a negation of the constitutional order. The remarks were then cited by opposition leaders to target Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary. No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution and I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution of India,” Bar and Bench quoted Justice Bhuyan as saying.He said the Constitution does not create two classes of citizens based on voting rights and added that wholesale disenfranchisement would violate Articles 326 and 14.“No authority can do it; no court can condone it. No one is above the Constitution,” he said.On deletion of names from electoral rolls, Bhuyan said, “Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing.From the persona of an Indian citizen, the right to vote or right to be included in the voters list cannot be detached. It will be like taking out the soul from the body.”Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said Bhuyan’s remarks showed that the CEC had violated the Constitution “both in letter and spirit”. “Justice Bhuyan has said much more and has exposed the CEC lock, stock and barrel. Gyanesh Kumar simply has lost all moral right to continue in office,” Ramesh said."Justice Ujjal Bhuyan, a sitting judge of the Supreme Court, has been an outspoken champion of environmental protection. Now the courageous jurist has forcefully expressed his view that the right to vote is very much part of the basic structure of the Constitution. This conclusively proves that the CEC—Constitutional functionary himself—has violated the Constitution itself both in letter and spirit," he said."Justice Bhuyan has said much more and has exposed the CEC lock, stock and barrel. Article Title: India can launch surgical strikes on Pakistan, but can't hold talks: Mani Shankar Aiyar
Article Text:

SRINAGAR: Former Union minister Mani Shankar Aiyar criticised the BJP-led central government for refusing to hold talks with Pakistan, saying it has the "courage" to launch surgical strikes but lacks the willingness to resolve issues.Speaking at the 5th Halla Bolle Conclave here, the Congress veteran suggested holding talks at the Attari-Wagah border, asserting that arguing over past issues was not foreign policy."We seem to have the courage to go into surgical strikes with them. Why don't we have the courage to sit across the table with them? Why can't we talk to them? Why can't we make friends with them?" he asked."Is there any other country in the world with whom we are more comfortable than with Pakistan? Is there any country in the world with whom Pakistan is more able to, you know, chat than with us?" he asked.Pointing to previous dialogue processes with Pakistan, Aiyar asked, "Why don't we show the courage to go there, and let them come here?""And if you don't have that courage, then my suggestion is that we meet at Wagah-Attari. Place a table right on our border line so that the Pakistani delegation doesn't leave Pakistan to talk to us, and we don't leave India to talk to them. And keep this dialogue going," he said.He said the dialogue can establish what can be resolved and what cannot be resolved."Wherever a resolution emerges, let us take action on that. And whatever hasn't been resolved, just postpone it, saying that for now it seems we cannot agree on this, but we will continue our dialogue. And whenever the atmosphere changes, then we will take up these remaining issues as well," he added.He, however, asserted that having arguments about the past was not foreign affairs."I think the only way we can arrive at any kind of constructive conclusion is by talking to them, however long it takes. And that is what the Americans did with the Russians. They never broke the diplomatic relationship; they never broke the dialogue. Sensible countries talk to each other; stupid countries don't talk to each other," he said.To a question about the political situation in the country, Aiyar said, 'It is very easy to fix what is wrong with the Indian political environment.""And to do that, you only have to follow the advice given by (PDP president) Mehbooba Mufti to Kashmiris, where she said that until all Kashmiris get together with a single voice, Delhi will not be influenced by individual Kashmiri leaders coming to Delhi," he said.The former Union minister added that the same can be said about the national political scene, which can be fixed when the entire non-Hindutva polity comes together."It can come together because we already have the INDIA bloc. And if the INDIA bloc comes together, we showed in the 2024 election that had we consolidated that bloc, we would have easily got the extra eight seats that are required to bring about a majority. And do you think Nitish would have joined him? Do you think Chandrababu would have joined him? No," he said."We would have been in Delhi, and Kashmir would have got back its statehood. Kashmir might even have received back Article 370 and 35A, perhaps in a slightly different shape. But if you want to make progress, those who disagree have to get together. And if we get together, then we can make new initiatives on Pakistan," he added.He emphasised that the Indian tradition is to talk."We need to talk to Srinagar, Srinagar needs to talk to Jammu, the street's voice needs to be brought into the discussion between the Government of India and the Government of Pakistan," he said.
Article Summary: Aiyar calls for india-pakistan talks, suggests meeting at wagah-attari border. Former union minister says india has the "courage" to launch surgical strikes but lacks the willingness to resolve issues. Congress veteran asserts that arguing over past issues was not foreign policy.

Article Title: Where will India be 5 to 10 years from now? EAM Jaishankar answers
Article Text:
During the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, S Jaishankar elaborated on India's potential to rise swiftly in the global power arena within the next decade.

India’s place among middle powers

Jaishankar’s wider power assessment

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

External affairs minister S Jaishankar said India has the potential to move rapidly up the global power hierarchy over the next five to 10 years, citing decades of high growth ahead, a supportive demographic profile and the emergence of new economic opportunities.Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi on Sunday, Jaishankar was asked where India would be positioned in the global order five to 10 years from now. He said countries currently classified as middle powers would not necessarily follow the same trajectory.“Some powers are more middle, and some are upper middle,” Jaishankar said. “Some of the powers have considerable and realistic potential even in the near short medium term to grow very rapidly.”Turning to India, Jaishankar said the country has “decades of high growth” ahead and argued that its demographic profile could help sustain that growth.“In the case of India, because we have decades of high growth ahead of us, and we have all said and done, a demography that will sustain that growth,” he said.Jaishankar also argued that India may not need to follow the traditional industrialisation path taken by earlier economies, pointing to the emergence of new possibilities in a rapidly changing global economy.“I would even argue, a world that is much more creative, where many new possibilities are there, so that we don't necessarily have to tread the earlier path of industrialization,” he said.“The orthodox path will have to devise something much more contemporary for what awaits us,” he added.Jaishankar said the global power hierarchy is likely to evolve unevenly, with countries currently grouped together as middle powers potentially moving in different directions.“Among the middle powers, some will peel off, some will stay put, some may drop down a bit,” he said.“That is the reality. That will be part of the evolution of the global order,” Jaishankar added.His remarks came during a wider discussion on the changing international power structure at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi. The meeting is being held on October 4 and 5 and brings together senior decision-makers and experts to discuss foreign and security policy issues.Earlier during the discussion, Jaishankar said the United States and China should not be viewed as middle powers, highlighting their vastly different levels of global influence.“When we say what the prospects are, we are also looking at an international landscape. As I said, what is important to define is what is not a middle power,” he said.On the US, Jaishankar said Washington has been the “underwriter of the global system for many decades” and has “a significant lead over any other power”.He then pointed to China’s economic strength, saying it accounts for “one third of the global manufacturing” and that its economic capabilities are translating into political influence.“This is really, in a sense, the subject matter of our discussion,” Jaishankar said.The Munich Leaders Meeting is a platform organised by the Munich Security Conference, a leading international forum on security and foreign policy. The New Delhi meeting on October 4 and 5 brings together senior decision-makers and experts from the Indo-Pacific, Europe and the US for discussions on major geopolitical, foreign and security policy issues.
Article Summary: During the munich leaders meeting in new delhi, s jaishankar elaborated on india's potential to rise swiftly in the global power arena within the next decade. He said countries currently classified as middle powers would not necessarily follow the same trajectory. His remarks came during a wider discussion on the changing international power structure.

NEW DELHI: Security forces on Sunday launched search operations in Jammu and Kashmir ’s Rajouri and Udhampur districts following inputs about suspected terrorist movement in forest areas.According to officials, the operation in Rajouri was launched after three suspected terrorists allegedly abducted a villager, Anil Sudan, near his house at Upper Lardia in the Sunderbani sector late Saturday night.The terrorists released Sudan around 3.15 am after using him as a guide to reach the Dua Khad forest, the officials said.Police and Army personnel rushed to the area after being alerted and launched a combing operation to trace the suspects. No contact has been established with them so far, officials said.Security forces also cordoned off the Mandugala Dhok forest in Rajouri after locals reported seeing two persons dressed in black and carrying backpacks and weapons.Another search operation is underway in Chigli Keya village in Udhampur, officials said.On September 17, two Pakistani terrorists were killed in an encounter with security forces in the Majalta area of Udhampur. One more terrorist was reportedly injured but managed to escape.This comes a day after ministry of external affairs summoned the Chargé d'Affaires of the Pakistan high commission to lodge a strong protest over what it described as the continued facilitation of illegal cross-border infiltration from Pakistan.India also urged Islamabad to investigate such infiltration and drug-smuggling activities, including the alleged involvement of Pakistani border forces, and take appropriate corrective measures."Pakistan was further urged to ensure respect for the sanctity of the International Border, strictly observe relevant bilateral arrangements, mandate its forces to exercise effective control to prevent unauthorized movement from its side, and take definitive measures to prevent the recurrence of such incidents," MEA said.
